explanation: Fires on a middle or later subword piece inside a rare, multi-token proper name or technical term (e.g. Gl-[ax]-oSmithKline, U-[dz]-ungwa, Psych-[od]-idae, Can-óvanas, Tam-iflu, down-conversion). The token only counts when it continues an unusual name the model is still spelling out. Common words and function words give weak or no activation.

A mixture of contexts with no shared theme: code-syntax spots such as the attribute-value opener =" after v-model, :class or ng-model, Elixir 'do', '(' in callbacks and package path pieces; math notation (~ N); and prose words like 'performance', 'electron' and 'hulk'. The token itself does not predict the activation well.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that the tokenizer splits, mostly a word-initial 'N'/'n' that starts an acronym or proper name (NCHC, Niterói, Nittany, NBL, Ntilikina, Nascar, Nodules, nuns). Weaker cases are other split-off word starts such as El-, Fl-, sn- and ran-. Whole common words do not fire it.

Fires most strongly on the preposition or word right after a reporting or announcing verb in news and legal prose ('said on Monday', 'announced on', 'argued in', 'said in a statement', 'joked on'). It also fires on unrelated boilerplate tokens: 'type' in <link rel=stylesheet type=...>, 'any' in 'free of charge, to any person', and C++ class export macros.

Fires on nouns, or the final subword of nouns, for bands or rings worn on or wrapped around something: belt, collar, scarf, cap, bikini, corset, bracelets, watchband, gastric band, seat-belted, annulus/annular, planetary rings. Related accessory or armor words fire moderately. Unrelated nouns are weak.

Fires on subword pieces in the middle of rare or foreign words and names (German, Hungarian, Persian, Vietnamese, drug names: Beitr-, hib-, doxyc-, ascor-, Djoh-). It also fires on spaces, digits and dots inside identifiers such as court case numbers ('NO. 02-'), model numbers ('Dell 922', 'BMP280') and version strings. Ordinary English words are weak.

Fires on the head noun or 'of' of a statistical or ranking quantity phrase: 'incidence rate', 'highest effect size', 'percent of', 'number of', 'frequency of', 'detection frequency', 'nearest', 'one of the first', 'ticket price', 'final step'. Activation is strongest when the token names the quantity that a number or comparison is about to fill in.

Fires on tokens that complete a strongly predictable fixed phrase or boilerplate span: 'derived from this software', 'throwing in the towel', 'tread on', 'jump to that section', 'If applicable', 'REVERSED AND RENDERED', 'revocable', 'travis-ci.org', 'stddef.h'. The tokens share no single meaning, so the unit seems to track collocation completion. That reading is uncertain.

Fires mainly on digits and hyphens inside bibliographic citations (page ranges like '565-577', volume/issue '2017;6:', reference IDs) and in product, model or version codes ('KDL-40HX803', 'rtl8723', 'Clinac 21'). A second, smaller group is the head word of team or club names ('Bombers Football Club', 'men's basketball team', 'Crytek Group').

Fires most strongly on the Go keyword 'package' at the start of a Go file, after the license or comments, and on other Go-ecosystem tokens (go-swagger, aws-sdk-go, fmt). It also fires on assorted unrelated name or word completions (Zelazny, dermal, jerky, Weyl, transcendental, a Chinese surname character).

Two unrelated groups. (1) Comparative or degree constructions: the token after 'more' ('more than/then', 'more the', 'more that') and 'long enough'. (2) The completing subword of scientific terms: pro-tons/pro-ton, asympt-otic, radio-therapy, random-ised, immunost-aining.

Fires on a word-initial Latinate prefix piece when the word is split into subwords, especially comp-/Com- (compromise, compelling, compulsory, Commissariat), and also dep-, prop-, extr-, disp-, impr-, intr-, diff-, con-, in English, Portuguese, Spanish and French. Whole words, and pieces that do not begin a word, fire weakly.

No consistent pattern. Top cases mix a name ending (Erdős and Tur-án), math symbols (=, $, ')'), code tokens (card:, models.), 'United States', 'letters' in probability questions, and assorted nouns. I can't predict new activations.

Fires on tokens in source code and software boilerplate: 'express' in 'either express or implied', 'CONTRACT' in MIT license text, and argument separators, backticks, indentation and identifiers inside code (SQL, JS, Go, PHP, XML schema). Activation needs a code or license context. Prose gives little.
